reading.body:
Microsoft operates a data center campus in West Des Moines spanning three counties in Iowa, with this Polk County facility as one component. The operator does not publish power capacity, square footage, or specific addresses for individual campuses, disclosing only aggregate worldwide statistics covering 500+ datacenters across 80+ Azure regions and 40+ gigawatts of contracted renewable energy. Any estimate of this campus's compute density therefore rests on Microsoft's reported $1.5–2 billion capital investment and plans for a sixth data center building, codenamed Ruthenium, but without published megawatts the scale cannot be read directly.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power capacity figures. This campus ranks third among Iowa facilities by disclosed megawatts, though that ranking reflects the state's overall lack of transparency rather than confirmed scale. The two facilities with published figures account for 18 MW total in the state, so the third-ranked campus—this one—has published capacity below that threshold or is intentionally undisclosed.

The West Des Moines campus matters to AI infrastructure planning primarily as a committed major investment by a hyperscaler with global AI deployment obligations, not as a quantified constraint on the grid or an identified point of AI compute concentration. Until Microsoft publishes individual campus capacity figures, this facility cannot be measured against other regional AI buildouts or ranked in its contribution to national compute growth.
